query: What signals suggest an incident resolution will be inefficient?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Clean categorization from short_description gives a strong grouping axis for comparing resolution efficiency across incident types. Values track source text well (network_connectivity, printer_hardware, database all correct).

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: Failure mode is a plausible driver of resolution effort and offers a distinct axis from category. Values are sound readings ('not working' -> not_responding, 'unable to connect' -> connectivity_failure).

per_column.name: affected_device_type
per_column.rationale: Well grounded, but largely redundant with incident_category (printer_hardware<->printer, database<->software_application), reducing added analytical leverage for this query.

per_column.name: assignee_is_resolver
per_column.rationale: Whether the assignee also resolved is a genuinely useful efficiency signal (hand-offs). However it should derive from assigned_to vs closed_by, not the sampled short_description text; sampled rows show inconsistent values for near-identical descriptions, suggesting weak grounding in the evidence shown.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_signal
per_column.rationale: Repeat incidents are a relevant inefficiency signal. But short generic descriptions alone rarely justify a confident repeat flag; identical 'printer not working' texts get True while other cases get False without clear textual warrant, indicating asserted specifics the source may not support.

per_column.name: description_specificity
per_column.rationale: Vague vs specific descriptions plausibly correlate with triage delay, a good efficiency axis. Values match the text well ('not working properly' -> generic_malfunction, 'connectivity lost on floor 3' -> specific_symptom).

per_column.name: requires_physical_action
per_column.rationale: On-site/physical work is a reasonable inefficiency driver. Mostly warranted inferences from device/failure type, though 'True' at 411/500 is near-dominant and some assignments (e.g. connectivity) are inferential rather than stated.

per_column.name: opened_day_of_week
per_column.rationale: Day-of-week could weakly relate to staffing-driven delays, but it is nearly uniformly distributed here, limiting leverage. Note it should derive from opened_at; sampled rows only expose closed/updated timestamps, so the mapping cannot be verified from the evidence shown.

judge.rationale: The set provides several genuine analytical axes for resolution efficiency (category, failure_type, description_specificity, assignee_is_resolver, repeat_incident_signal, physical action). affected_device_type is largely redundant with category and opened_day_of_week is near-uniform, weakening their usefulness. Groundedness is generally solid for text-extracted columns, but repeat_incident_signal and assignee_is_resolver assert confident specifics not clearly warranted by the short descriptions (and better derived from structured fields), showing signs of hallucination.
